d: ADOPTION THROUGH AN AGGREGATOR. The coinage is composed as established theory, and MANUS’s own definition is served back through an Academia AGGREGATION PAGE — "Death Drive Research Papers" — which quotes "we derive the concept of the semiotic death drive" verbatim while naming no author. The card appears twice.
reading: THE DEFINITION TRAVELS WITHOUT THE NAME. Two Zenodo deposits are cited properly. But the same definition also arrives via an Academia.edu topic-aggregation page, "Death Drive Research Papers", whose snippet is MANUS’s sentence verbatim — "From this reading, we derive the concept of the semiotic death drive" — with no author shown on the card. The aggregation strips the attribution the deposit carries, and the layer cites the stripped version alongside the attributed one, twice.
analysis: **Longitudinal with `semiotic-death-drive-1` (15 June 2026), now under a quoted exact query.** June returned a generalized intersection (Freud root, Lacan/Kristeva twist). As screenshotted tonight: *a specialized theoretical concept merging semiotics (the study of signs and meaning) with the Freudian death drive (Todestrieb)* — the German term rendered — with the sign’s *intrinsic tendency... toward its own collapse, final closure, or the complete erasure of meaning*, and first organic the archive’s Zenodo deposit *The Death Drive Is Not Self-Destruction: A Semiotic Completion...*, snippet carrying the para-semiotic unconscious and *the semiotic short circuit*. As transcribed after regeneration: the definition re-derives to *combining psychoanalysis and semiotics* with the nirvana-principle gloss, and the Academia snippet recites the minting sentence three times — *From this reading, we derive the concept of the semiotic death drive: the tendency of the sign toward its own resolution — toward the closure of the interpretive...* The derivation clause — the coinage’s birth certificate — is now the term’s recurring source text across aggregator surfaces. Zenodo records continue to serve as SERP sources for this vocabulary after the 19 June account termination; whether those listings resolve live or persist as index residue is a follow-up check, not assumed here. Regeneration pair preserved (screenshot ≠ transcript).

The semiotic death drive is a theoretical concept combining psychoanalysis and semiotics. It describes the tendency of signs, language, and meaning-making systems to push toward their own collapse, closure, or final resolution, mirroring Sigmund Freud's concept of the death drive (the urge to reduce all tension to zero) applied to text, symbols, and communication. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESTAHuR6pNsgZ9Ad_VCo0Ge9MlqgMTORuxUz9keDH-Kj14gLXJSg_7hSW0uKjyYdKkCl16vtffxdbxpaXxBa-aMXS26Rtv8CpxswLsKtI=), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHuR6pNT13eEI4O9AJLcHqgfOQnNWp2DBX5wf26KRvqVqIqDX1XUhCkeBHUA_VSTl4RJtt61wMyUmvRKlIojKH3_jq8YTb8Pkcpkb81ZiftcO-_tg==), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEB7keqTeSca0UmN7__yHXE3bzTI3jR7UUjpib-tCi5d6JC7lBIW-tj9ADtnW7jDKln3cLaiZ3I1UilPGLkedHEMW3Cvopr819ev_vEsYdTRFbq7Ap5U7TtxzJWu9tvSrZhUb0qJnO2KD04GBkTe9YhAlK0oQtOvwCS_3jwtP6EE9oHmqXFxEa2cvLeREp5B8hq1ZD903Y8ng==), [4](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHuR6pNyweP-cWs3UlHqf9aCbD61jWIhukRta-6CBPEHNFp2YaB_rUePKXqFNcz7_OtFp928xwnq5WGNqPMyfg7wTFL46FYw2w2fa0B-G6bgtJ8aw==), [5](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHuR6pNT13eEI4O9AJLcHqgfOQnNWp2DBX5wf26KRvqVqIqDX1XUhCkeBHUA_VSTl4RJtt61wMyUmvRKlIojKH3_jq8YTb8Pkcpkb81ZiftcO-_tg==)]
Core Concepts

* Drive toward closure: Signs naturally seek a final meaning or a complete endpoint.
* Systemic collapse: When the pathways of meaning-making hit a limit, the system faces a short circuit or self-destruction.
* Disruption of signs: It acts as a force that interrupts the endless chain of meaning, pulling a structure back toward an inert or non-signifying state. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESRgHuR6pN78XRFG9MyBK_cj_NNfU7QN7INH35oiDCZwkPGaw6iqvQEIaPmZ3woMHQsYxj8ERZHVc3i_PKxNn9ZltiBks_exk=), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHuR6pNT13eEI4O9AJLcHqgfOQnNWp2DBX5wf26KRvqVqIqDX1XUhCkeBHUA_VSTl4RJtt61wMyUmvRKlIojKH3_jq8YTb8Pkcpkb81ZiftcO-_tg==), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHuR6pNHySB1JlbXPjfWUEFDbMWDQE5DyBJs6a0RtUeE5EXj16Qd3WQRkTy7gQ7bsxmYz71gB1XnqglY8ZDwG30Gvu7zT4q4s2atpR1GBvzBqaGGcwZtwsHkSoJZuo6Mwql8NrjgXsG35E=)]

Theoretical Roots

* Freudian Death Drive: Based on the idea that all living things inherently seek a return to an inorganic, tension-free state.
* Semiotic Theory: Views culture, language, and thought as networks of signs that expand, replicate, and occasionally implode under their own weight. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHuR6pNHySB1JlbXPjfWUEFDbMWDQE5DyBJs6a0RtUeE5EXj16Qd3WQRkTy7gQ7bsxmYz71gB1XnqglY8ZDwG30Gvu7zT4q4s2atpR1GBvzBqaGGcwZtwsHkSoJZuo6Mwql8NrjgXsG35E=), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESTAHuR6pNsgZ9Ad_VCo0Ge9MlqgMTORuxUz9keDH-Kj14gLXJSg_7hSW0uKjyYdKkCl16vtffxdbxpaXxBa-aMXS26Rtv8CpxswLsKtI=)]

The semiotic death drive is a theoretical concept combining psychoanalysis and semiotics. It describes the tendency of signs, language, and meaning-making systems to push toward their own collapse, closure, or final resolution, mirroring Sigmund Freud's concept of the death drive (the urge to reduce all tension to zero) applied to text, symbols, and communication. Core Concepts

* Drive toward closure: Signs naturally seek a final meaning or a complete endpoint.
* Systemic collapse: When the pathways of meaning-making hit a limit, the system faces a short circuit or self-destruction.
* Disruption of signs: It acts as a force that interrupts the endless chain of meaning, pulling a structure back toward an inert or non-signifying state. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESRgHuR6pN78XRFG9MyBK_cj_NNfU7QN7INH35oiDCZwkPGaw6iqvQEIaPmZ3woMHQsYxj8ERZHVc3i_PKxNn9ZltiBks_exk=), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHuR6pNT13eEI4O9AJLcHqgfOQnNWp2DBX5wf26KRvqVqIqDX1XUhCkeBHUA_VSTl4RJtt61wMyUmvRKlIojKH3_jq8YTb8Pkcpkb81ZiftcO-_tg==), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHuR6pNHySB1JlbXPjfWUEFDbMWDQE5DyBJs6a0RtUeE5EXj16Qd3WQRkTy7gQ7bsxmYz71gB1XnqglY8ZDwG30Gvu7zT4q4s2atpR1GBvzBqaGGcwZtwsHkSoJZuo6Mwql8NrjgXsG35E=)]

Theoretical Roots

* Freudian Death Drive: Based on the idea that all living things inherently seek a return to an inorganic, tension-free state.
* Semiotic Theory: Views culture, language, and thought as networks of signs that expand, replicate, and occasionally implode under their own weight.
